title: Direct Imaging of Field-induced Modulation of Two-dimensional Electron Gas at LaAlO3/SrTiO3 Interface by Polar Distortion of LaAlO3
content: In the quest for advanced nanoelectronic devices, oxide interfaces have emerged as pivotal platforms because of their diverse electronic and structural properties. One of the most prominent examples is the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 (LAO/STO) interface, which hosts a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) confined to within a few unit cells [1]. This 2DEG not only exhibits high carrier density and mobility but also reveals intriguing properties such as superconductivity, magnetism, and strong spin-orbit coupling, all within a controllable oxide framework. While the 2DEG’s basic formation mechanism–arising from the polar discontinuity at the LAO/STO interface–is relatively well understood, a gap remains in understanding precisely how the 2DEG responds to electrical biasing, especially regarding the interplay between polar distortions in the oxide lattice and the motion of oxygen vacancies (VO) [2].
